content:
Alicia Perez: For the unit economics dashboard cost charts — we need to align on formatting/rounding so people don’t over-interpret noise. Specifically for blended $/1M output tokens and the drilldown tables.

Alicia Perez: Questions:
1) Units: show as `$ / 1M output tokens` everywhere? Or `$ per 1M` shorthand.
2) Rounding: 2 decimals? 1 decimal? Dynamic based on magnitude?
3) When data coverage is incomplete (missing region/tier/model tags) do we show a confidence indicator? If yes, how?

Felix Schneider: +1. Right now the chart y-axis in my local build is `$0.00`-style, which makes the line look super spiky when it’s just like +0.03.

Nora Ahmed: Also tables: sorting by “$ / 1M” but we’re displaying 2 decimals -> lots of ties / looks like random ordering.

Chloe Martin: Eng preference: pick a consistent display rule; we can still keep full precision in hover + export. But the default view needs to prevent “oh no we went from 1.21 to 1.22 = regression” reactions.

Allison Grant: From observability side, I’d really like some way to indicate when the metric is partial. We’re going to have gaps early on (streaming parity + backfills). Even a “Coverage: 97%” badge would help.

Alicia Perez: Proposed direction (tell me if this is sane):
- Primary display: `$X.XX / 1M output tokens` in charts + KPI tiles, but apply **significant-figures-ish rounding**.
- Show **absolute** in tooltips at higher precision (like 4 decimals) + show % change with a guardrail.
- Add a small “Data quality” pill near the chart title: `Good` / `Partial` / `Delayed` with hover explaining why.

Felix Schneider: What’s the scale typically? Are we talking $0.50 vs $5.00? Because 2 decimals means different things.

Rishi Malhotra: Jumping in w/ finance lens: we should avoid implying precision that we don’t have. For blended cost, a change of a few basis points can be within normal allocation variance (idle + overhead). I’d prefer 2 decimals max, and ideally show a delta threshold before we color it red/green.

Alicia Perez: Ok so maybe:
- If value >= 10: show 1 decimal (e.g., $12.3)
- 1 to <10: show 2 decimals (e.g., $3.47)
- <1: show 3 decimals (e.g., $0.823)
Still display `/ 1M` so people don’t confuse it with $/token.

Nora Ahmed: That helps. For the tiny numbers, 0.823 vs 0.82 matters visually.

Chloe Martin: Implementation-wise we can do a formatter that returns `display_value` + `raw_value` for tooltip. The API currently returns a float; UI can format.

Allison Grant: For confidence indicator — can we tie it to our pipeline checks? E.g., if freshness SLO violated or missing_dimension_rate > threshold => “Partial”. Otherwise “Good”.

Alicia Perez: Yes. UX idea: small dot + label next to the metric name.
- Green dot `Good` (>= 99% coverage, within freshness SLO)
- Yellow dot `Partial` (coverage < 99% OR some dimensions missing)
- Gray dot `Delayed` (freshness behind)
Hover: “Coverage is based on % of requests with complete dimensions and presence of hourly partitions.”

Felix Schneider: +1 but please don’t block the chart if Partial. Just show the label and maybe an info icon.

Rishi Malhotra: For exec readouts, I’d like the default time granularity and formatting to be stable. Can we also add a note somewhere that this is “blended cost” and includes idle + overhead per ADR? People keep comparing it to marginal.

Alicia Perez: Good call. I’ll add an inline helper text under the KPI tile: “Blended includes allocated overhead and idle capacity. See methodology.” (link)

Nora Ahmed: Another gotcha: % change indicators. If you show “+0.8% WoW” people treat it as real. Can we add a minimum change threshold before we show arrows/colors?

Alicia Perez: Suggest:
- Only show colored delta if abs(% change) >= 2% OR abs($ change) >= $0.10 / 1M (whichever triggers)
- Otherwise show delta in muted gray.

Chloe Martin: Works. Also: do we smooth the line? Finance asked for hourly granularity but it looks noisy. I’d rather keep raw points but default to daily rollup for the main view.

Rishi Malhotra: Daily by default, yes. Hourly available as a toggle for debugging.

Allison Grant: If daily default, then the “Delayed” status should be relative to the daily partition cutoff (timezone matters). We’ve had day-boundary confusion.

Alicia Perez: On timezone: we’ll label the chart “UTC” or “PST”?

Chloe Martin: For internal tools I’d pick UTC for consistency with warehouse partitions. But we can show tooltip with local time too.

Felix Schneider: +1 UTC. Also: y-axis tick labels — can we avoid `$0.00` repeated? Use compact: `$1.2`, `$1.4` etc.

Alicia Perez: Yep. Y-axis ticks compact to 1 decimal unless <1.

Alicia Perez: Summary for DES-319 notes:
- Unit label: always `$ / 1M output tokens`.
- Dynamic rounding: >=10 (1 dec), 1–<10 (2 dec), <1 (3 dec). Tooltip shows 4 dec.
- Delta coloring threshold: >=2% OR >=$0.10 / 1M; else muted.
- Default granularity: daily; hourly toggle.
- Add “Data quality” status pill: Good/Partial/Delayed based on pipeline coverage + freshness checks; non-blocking with hover details.
- Add helper text: “Blended includes allocated overhead + idle; link to methodology.”

Nora Ahmed: Looks good. Can you also specify table formatting? Same rounding rules in top-N tables + keep raw on hover.

Alicia Perez: Yep, same rules. Table cells show formatted; hover shows raw + coverage % for that row if Partial.

Allison Grant: If you want, I can provide the exact labels from the alerting side so the pill maps 1:1. We already compute completeness and freshness.

Chloe Martin: Please do. If you can drop the metric names / thresholds we can wire it in.

Allison Grant: Will follow up in eng-sre thread w/ names. Here’s the quick version:
- completeness_pct
- missing_dimension_pct
- freshness_lag_minutes
We can derive status in the backend or UI.

Alicia Perez: Great. I’ll update the design spec + add examples so reviewers see before/after. Thanks all.
